title: Session stabilizer proxy & traffic normalizer for cross-SDK VCR/contract suite
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current VCR/mockserver cassettes are brittle across SDKs (Python/TS/Go) when run in CI because small runtime differences (timestamps, ephemeral session IDs, header ordering, and chunked streaming boundaries) cause spurious failures. This makes contract tests noisy, increases flakiness in release gates, and slows down PR velocity for SDK changes that don't affect the API semantics.

Goal: Implement a lightweight local 'session stabilizer' proxy that sits between SDK test runners and the real Redwood API during initial cassette capture and a corresponding normalization transform that runs at cassette-replay time. The proxy should: (1) deterministically normalize session identifiers and ephemeral headers, (2) merge/align streaming frame boundaries for consistent VCR snapshots, (3) optionally pad or trim timing metadata used by SDKs for retry/backoff logic, and (4) produce augmented metadata used by contract assertions (e.g., canonicalized request fingerprint, inferred compatibility-level). The implementation must be language-agnostic (HTTP-level) and configurable by cassette/recording metadata so each SDK can opt into different normalization levels.

Why different from prior work: Existing mockserver/VCR fixtures in the repo focus on deterministic replay and retry simulation but do not address cross-language normalization of streaming events or session-level hashing. This ticket builds a normalization layer that complements the VCR cassette format (no change to vendor cassettes required) and reduces duplicate cassette variants across SDKs and environments.
acceptance_criteria: A session stabilizer proxy binary (or lightweight Python/Go script) runs locally and can record a canonicalized cassette when pointed at the Redwood staging API
Captured cassettes contain a normalized metadata block: canonical_request_hash, session_map (stable IDs), streaming_boundaries (aligned), and capture-version
Replaying a stabilized cassette against the mock proxy yields identical byte-for-byte responses across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK CI runners for the same recorded scenario
Integration tests added: streaming backpressure scenario, chunked-chunk-boundary mismatch, and retry-after header variation all pass deterministically in CI
Documentation: README with usage examples for python-sdk/ts-sdk/go-sdk and a short migration guide for existing cassettes
design_notes:
Key considerations: (1) Do NOT change app-level payloads; normalization is strictly metadata and ordering of frames only. (2) Provide a pluggable sanitizer chain (header normalizer, session hasher, frame re-chunker, timing scrubber). (3) Keep the proxy single-threaded and focused on test harness use; production traffic routing not a goal. (4) Store canonicals in cassette metadata under 'x-redwood-stabilizer' so existing VCR parsers ignore unknown keys if not opted in.

Options considered: embedding normalizer logic inside each SDK vs a single external proxy. Chosen: external proxy to avoid repeated SDK changes and reduce language-specific bugs. We may later provide small SDK helpers to toggle normalization levels via environment variables.

Security: proxy only used against staging/test endpoints. We add a short section to README about not using it with production credentials and provide a flag to strip Authorization headers from recorded cassettes.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (this ticket): prototype proxy + normalization rules, record 3 canonical cassettes (simple generation, streaming chat with function calls, retry/backoff sequence). Phase 2: add CI integration wrappers for python/ts/go SDK test suites and a lint step that rejects non-stabilized cassette uploads. Phase 3 (follow-up): optional server-side canonicalizer to dedupe existing cassette corpus.

Tech notes: prototype in Go for single-binary distribution (easy to run in CI), use net/http reverse proxy, middleware for normalization. Store cassettes in existing VCR format with a new metadata block. Provide small CLI subcommands: record, replay-normalize, inspect.

Telemetry: emit a short stable hash per cassette to help tracking duplicate failures across tests.
test_matrix:
Scenarios to validate:
- Non-streaming request/response with ephemeral session ID and authorization header differences.
- Streaming chat: different chunking across SDKs (TS: 1 chunk per event, Python: buffered chunks) -> must align events.
- Retry and backoff: varied X-Request-Start timestamps and Retry-After jitter -> normalized timing scrubbed unless test opts into timing-preservation.
- Header ordering variations and additional SDK-specific headers are stripped or canonicalized.
Each scenario must be run in Python 3.11, Node 20, and Go 1.21 CI containers.
